title: Design System: How We Met — Florida

display.purpose: Desktop introduction title; narrow and short-screen overrides remain in Florida CSS.

body.purpose: Introduction sentences; dialogs and supporting text use smaller observed sizes.

action.purpose: Primary start, resume, and replay controls.

chapter-title.purpose: Quicksand on the homepage Florida link only; does not change Toronto typography.

motion.name: introduction-shade
motion.purpose: Shade fades away when racing begins.

motion.name: caption-fade
motion.purpose: Callout departure after its runtime duration.

motion.name: boost-state
motion.purpose: Yellow fuel turns cream during boost.

motion.name: impact-flash
motion.purpose: Brief peripheral feedback, skipped for reduced motion.

motion.name: camera-follow
motion.purpose: Smooth chase camera; reduced motion disables boost expansion and shake.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Removes CSS transitions, flashes, shake, and hull bob/roll/pitch. World, fan, pickups, some character motion, and camera following continue.

components.name: Primary Race Button
components.description: Start, resume, and replay action; includes loading, hover, press, focus, and reduced-motion states.

components.name: Race Clock
components.description: Dense navy backing keeps tabular timing legible against moving sky and water. The sample pace matches the reviewed core configuration.

components.name: Nina Caption
components.description: Short, polite live commentary; runtime controls its opacity and duration.

components.name: Florida Chapter Link
components.description: Homepage-only bridge into Florida. Its Quicksand text preserves Toronto's existing page typography.

Next stop: Florida

You, Nina, an airboat, and the Intracoastal.

Play the 3D race →

narrative.overview:
Florida is a sunny, playful 3D place to race through with Barron and Nina. Faceted characters, warm waterfront buildings, palm silhouettes, and animated turquoise water carry the experience. The interface is a small set of arcade instruments: substantial type, clear controls, and room to see the course.

This record applies to florida/ and the Florida chapter link on the homepage. Its descriptive language follows the user-approved cute 3D Intracoastal brief. Toronto keeps its pixel art, Press Start 2P, and Quicksand; Florida's tokens are not global Toronto rules.
keyCharacteristics: Original low-poly geometry with warm daylight and visible material facets.
Cream and navy instruments, yellow actions, and coral accents.
Motion expressed through steering, wakes, the fan, and the couple.
A finish composition that includes the couple, bridge, and Fisheries.

rules.name: The Chapter Boundary Rule
rules.body: Extend these tokens within Florida; retain the homepage's Quicksand for its chapter link.

rules.name: The Moving Background Rule
rules.body: Keep the race clock and sector label on their navy instrument plates. Text shadows alone do not replace these surfaces.

rules.name: The Instrument Type Rule
rules.body: Use Bungee for short race titles and numbers; use Nunito for sentences, controls, and captions.

rules.name: The Arrival Rule
rules.body: Keep the couple, the 17th Street bridge, and Fisheries visible together beside the desktop result panel, including the reviewed 989px viewport.

dos: Keep the couple, course, hazards, and arrival landmarks readable.
Build Florida scenery and characters as coherent, faceted 3D forms.
Pair color-coded states with text, visible geometry, or both.
Preserve keyboard focus, pause behavior, and the honest phone-controls message.
Use the approved surface brief and current runtime as visual evidence.
donts: Apply Florida's fonts, palette, or 3D art rules to Toronto.
Replace live gameplay or the world background with the concept image.
Remove the navy backing from the race clock or sector label.
Describe responsive layouts as shipped touch controls.
Hide the couple or either arrival landmark behind the desktop result panel.
